title: From Tripods to Bipods Reducing the Queue Number of Planar Graphs Costs Just One Leg

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition 3.2 (Property P2b) and Lemma 3.3, as used in the proof of Theorem 3.4 (both the triangular and the quadrangular iterative step)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Definition 3.2 requires the connecting edge of a bipod to join the *shallowest* endpoints of the two vertical paths ('if both P1 and P2 are non-empty (u_{s_u}, v_{s_v}) ∈ E', with u_i, v_i ∈ L_i, i.e. index = layer), and Lemma 3.3 accordingly truncates the paths from the shallow side (choosing i, j 'maximally' and keeping P'_1 = (u_i, …, u_{t_u})). However, in the construction of Theorem 3.4 the bipod is built from the paths that run from the deep vertices v_1, v_2 (resp. t_1, t_3) *up* to the boundary roots p_1, p_2 (resp. p_1, p_3), with the connecting edge (v_1,v_2) at the deepest end and the shallow ends being precisely the vertices adjacent to p_1, p_2. Applying Lemma 3.3 as stated would delete exactly those shallow vertices, so the claim 'such an acyclic bipod still induces a path that can be extended by p_1 and p_3 to obtain a path connecting p_1 and p_3' (and the analogous claim in the triangular case) is false, and the new bag would no longer touch the bags on the boundary of C_f as required for CR1/CR2 and for splitting C_f. Either Definition 3.2(P2b) must use (u_{t_u}, v_{t_v}) and Lemma 3.3 must truncate from the deep side (minimal i, j, keeping P'_1 = (u_{s_u}, …, u_i)), or the construction is invalid.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3, iterative step for a quadrangular face f = (x1,x2,x3,x4): definition of edges e2 and e4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'if there is an edge e2 = (v_{k+1}, v2), where v_{k+1} ∈ B_{x_{k+1}} and v2 ∈ B_{x3}, we also connect x_{k+1} to x2. Similarly, if there is an edge e4 = (v_{k+1}, v2), where v_{k+1} ∈ B_{x_{k+1}} and v2 ∈ B_{x3}, we also connect x_{k+1} to x2.' Both sentences are identical and both wrongly refer to B_{x3}: e2 must be an edge to a vertex of B_{x2} (justifying the H-edge (x_{k+1}, x2)) and e4 must be an edge to a vertex of B_{x4} (justifying the H-edge (x_{k+1}, x4)). The subsequent text indeed uses e4 to create faces f_{14} = (x1,x4,x_{k+1}) and f_{43} = (x4,x3,x_{k+1}), which require the H-edge (x_{k+1}, x4) that was never introduced by the stated rule, so the definition contradicts its later use.

The reference list contains an unresolved citation key '?', i.e. one of the claimed follow-up works is not actually cited/present in the bibliography. The supporting evidence for the claim of a 'plethora of follow-up works' is therefore incomplete/unverifiable.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Lemma 4.1 (base case / inductive step boundary)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof handles the base case 'For n_f = 1 …' and then writes 'Hence, assume that n_f > 2.' This leaves the case n_f = 2 uncovered by both the base case and the inductive step; the assumption should be n_f ≥ 2 (equivalently n_f > 1) for the induction to be complete.
